chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, from Al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Aqeeqa, he said: 'The mother should not eat anything from it.'

key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةِ: Aqeeqa, the ritual sacrifice offered for a newborn child

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the mother eating from the Aqeeqa sacrifice?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a specific legal ruling in Shia jurisprudence that the mother of the newborn is prohibited from consuming any part of the Aqeeqa sacrifice. While the Prophet and other Imams often ate from their own Aqeeqa, this narration highlights a distinct practice or ruling for the mother, reflecting the nuanced scholarly discussions on whether this prohibition is specific to her or derived from the general principle that Aqeeqa is a gift (hadiya) rather than obligatory charity (sadaqah).
